info.name: SambaSafety API Documentation
info.description:
Welcome to our developer portal. This portal contains all the tools and resources you need to build and integrate our capabilities into your own projects. Whether you're a seasoned developer or just getting started, our portal makes it easy to take advantage of the powerful functionality our software has to offer. With detailed documentation, sample code, and technical support, you'll be able to get up and running in no time.

The endpoints documented are available for our customers to do custom integrations for complex workflows and processing.

Common Design Considerations

The following are some common design considerations when integrating with the API.

Dates

Dates are represented as strings in the ISO 8601 format. This format is both human-readable and easily parsed by machines. Here’s an example of a date string in ISO 8601 format:

 {
     "date": "2024-09-20",
     "datatime": "2024-09-20T10:56:33-07:00"
 }

Format:

  • YYYY: Four-digit year (e.g., 2024)

  • MM: Two-digit month (01-12)

  • DD: Two-digit day of the month (01-31)

  • T: Separator indicating the start of the time component

  • hh: Two-digit hour (00-23)

  • mm: Two-digit minute (00-59)

  • ss: Two-digit second (00-59)

  • Z: Indicates UTC time (can also be a timezone offset like +00:00)

License Number Patterns

For more information on License Number Formats visit the SambaSafety Knowledge Base:

  • US Driver License Number Formats

  • Canadian Driver License Number Formats

Gender

Acceptable Values
MALE
FEMALE
NON-BINARY

Email Address

An email must be a valid email address, and can contain the following special characters: +,.,-,_,@

EyeColor

Acceptable Values
BLACK
BLUE
BROWN
DICHROMATIC
GRAY
GREEN
HAZEL
PINK

License Category

Acceptable Values
ID
PERMIT
LICENSE

Purpose

Acceptable Values
INSURANCE
EMPLOYMENT
RESELLER_INSURANCE
RESELLER_EMPLOYMENT

Driver Name

The first, middle, and last name values may not contain special characters other than a hyphen - between family surnames OR apostrophe.

Unacceptable characters: á, é, í, ó, ú, ñ, ü,

Suffix

The suffix field does not accept comma's or periods.

Acceptable Values
JR
SR
II
III
IIII

Social Security Numbers

The ssn parameter accepts the 000000000 or 0000 numeric formats. You may need to remove - characters, when formatting this parameter.

Error Handling

The following documentation identifies the common error codes and messages you may encounter when interacting with our API endpoints. There are three main categories of error types we can return from our API. These errors include:

  • 4XX Client Side Errors

  • 5XX Server Side Errors

  • Application Errors

General Validation Rules

  • Required Fields: A 4XX client side error will be returned if a request is made that does not include all required properties.

  • Provided Fields are Invalid: A 4XX client sidde error will be returned if a request is made with an invalid property formats.

  • Provided Fields are Invalid for State: An application error will be returned if a request is made and the license number format does not match the state requirement.

This lists errors by their HTTP status codes as defined in RFC 7231.

4XX Client Side Errors

4XX client side errors can be corrected and resubmitted to the application.

400 Bad Request

A 400 bad request error is an HTTP status code that indicates that a application is unable to process a request due to a client’s malformed request.

Causes:

  • Malformed request syntax; For example, a missing comma or { }.

  • Invalid request body message; For example, a missing required property.

  • Typos in the URL

Suggested Action: Check the request, and retry.

401 Unauthorized / 403 Forbidden

The 401 Unauthorized error is an HTTP status code that indicates a client side error when a request to a web server is unsuccessful due to missing or incorrect authentication credentials. The 403 Forbidden is a similar HTTP status code, but the client does not have permissions to perform a certain action.

Causes:

  • You do not have valid credentials (Bearer Token)

  • Trying to access unauthorized data

Suggested Action: The most common reason for this is an expired bearer token, re-authenticate to refresh your token.

404 Not Found

The 404 Not Found error is an HTTP status code that indicates the server is unable to find the requested resource at a specific endpoint.

Causes:

  • A resource has been deleted or moved, or is temporary unavailable.

Suggested Action: Check the resource id, and retry. If still not found, check resource has not been deleted or moved.

406 Not Acceptable

This response is sent when the application doesn't find a matching Content-Type for the requested `Accepted` header.

Causes:

  • An invalid content-type was sent in the Acceptheader.

Suggested Action: Check the Acceptbeing sent in the header, and retry.

409 Conflict

This response is sent when a request conflicts with the current state of the application data.

Causes:

  • A property in the request body causes a property conflict in the application.

Suggested Action: Correct the property value as indicated in the error message, and retry.

422 Unprocessable Content

The request was well-formed but the application was unable process due to semantic errors.

Causes:

  • A property in the request body causes invalid property values in the application.

Suggested Action: Correct the property value as indicated in the error message, and retry.

429 Too Many Requests

This status code indicates to the client to slow down the rate of requests is commonly called "rate limiting".

Causes:

  • The client has sent too many requests in a given amount of time.

Suggested Action: Adjust your application's rate of requests being sent.

4XX Error Messages

Generated based on business/domain rules. An example of an error code returned when the characters submitted in the license state field didn’t match the required format.

{
    "code": "B02",
    "message": "Format for field(s) licenseState are invalid"
}

Generated by the application framework in some scenarios. An example is outlined below

{   
    "timestamp": "2024-04-11T18:16:28.810+00:00",   
    "status": 404,   
    "error": "Not Found",   
    "path": "/v1/mvrorxxxx"   
}
Error Code Error Description
B01 Required field(s) ‘’ are missing.
B02 Formats for field(s) ‘field names>’ are invalid.
B03 Person in archived status cannot be enrolled in monitoring.
Person xxxxx has already been matched.
Report type xxxx not supported
Unknown field xxxxxx in request body
C01 Provided call back URL is invalid
E01 Driver data is invalid, please fix and try again. invalid.
L01 License already assigned to a person.
R01 Required fields cannot be updated ‘’.
U01 Person already exists in group with field(s)
U02 License and State combination already exists.

5XX Server Side Errors

5XX server side errors can be resubmitted unchanged to the application after a short period of time.

500 Internal Server Error

The application has encountered a situation it does not know how to handle.

502 Bad Gateway

This error response means that the application, while working as a gateway to get a response needed to handle your request, got an invalid response.

503 Service Unavailable

The application is not ready to handle the request. Common causes are a server that is down for maintenance or that is overloaded.

504 Gateway Timeout

This error response is given when the application does not response in time.

Application Errors

Applications errors are returned with the normal HTTP 200 OK response code. These are successfully submitted requests that during the application’s workflow returns a backend error message.

Order Errors

Order errors can occur when the request doesn’t meet a state's requirements. Some examples include:

  • ordering a product not available for in that particular state.

  • not having a state-access code correctly configured in your request. (UT, CA, PA)

  • ordering an online vs overnight product (HI)

For more information on MVR Order Errors visit the SambaSafety Knowledge Base

No-Hit Errors

To determine whether it is a no‐hit error, look for a value of N in the Valid property of the Result object. If found, look for one of the values listed below in the ErrorDescription property.

JSON 2.0.4 Driver Not Found Example Response

{
    "Record": {
        "DlRecord": {
            "Criteria": {
                ...
            },
            "Result": {
                "Control": "07GRG8",
                "Valid": "N",
                "ErrorCode": "A2",
                "ErrorDescription": "DRIVER NOT FOUND",
                "ReturnedDate": {...},
                "ReturnedTime": {...},
                "CompanyClass": "NO RECORD FOUND AT THE DMV",
                "CompanyScore": "2",
                "CompanyScoreInt": 2,
                "CompanyVersion": "1-13",
                "ReklamiErrorCode": "MV",
                "ResultCode": "RC",
                "Designation": "ERROR"
            }
        }
    }
}

JSON 3.0.0 Driver Not Found Example Response

{
    "mvrId": "c2c489c5-6629-4cb0-8bc7-30ba33076507",
    "controlNumber": "HV0W0W",
    "mvrOrder": {
        "orderDateTime": "2024-08-08T06:53:00-07:00",
        "person": {
            "firstName": "JOHN",
            "lastName": "PUBLIC",
            "birthDate": "1980-10-19"
        },
        "license": {
            "licenseNumber": "C012345678",
            "licenseState": "CO"
        }
    },
    "mvrOrderResult": {
        "orderDateTime": "2024-08-08T06:53:00-07:00",
        "productID": "DL",
        "valid": "N",
        "response": "LICENSE AND NAME OR DOB DO NOT MATCH",
        "returnedDateTime": "2024-08-08T06:53:00-07:00"
    }
}

SYSTEM IS DOWN

Unfortunately there are times when the application is down. Network issues, system updates, and planned maintenance times can cause a system down response.

For more information on MVR Platform Status visit the SambaSafety Knowledge Base

JSON 2.0.4 System Down Example Response

{
    "Record": {
        "DlRecord": {
            "Criteria": {
                ...
            },
            "Result": {
                "Control": "07GRG9",
                "Valid": "N",
                "ErrorCode": "ZD",
                "ErrorDescription": "SYSTEM IS DOWN",
                "ReturnedDate": {...},
                "ReturnedTime": {...},
                "ResultCode": "13",
                "Designation": ""
            }
        }
    }
}

Getting Started

This collection can be used with your SambaSafety credentials in both our Demo or Production environments. We offer this collection publicly to assist you in implementing your solution with our APIs. It's meant to jump start your exploration.

This collection can be forked, copied or imported into your own team workspace.

Mock Examples

SambaSafety has a demo system that will allow you to simulate the process of sending orders and getting reports during your development phase. This environment contains sample data that will allow you to verify the entire process without actually incurring state fees charges. Our demo environment will simulate the same connectivity/security behavior you will encounter when you send orders to our production system.

In addition, you will be able to exercise error handling and token management. This system is not designed to facilitate stress testing. This environment is completely independent of our production system, so your demo account credentials will contain a different account than your production account.

Once you have your demo system credentials you are free to begin connecting to our demo environment.

Environment Variables

Here are some best practices to follow when you demo and share APIs with customers:

  • Ensure that no API keys are exposed during the demo. Always use environment variables for authentication.

  • When sharing environments with customers, ensure it doesn't contain any API keys.

  • If you need to share the same collection with customers repeatedly, consider sharing it using a public workspace. Alternatively, you can export and share collections and environments.

This collection looks for these environment variables. You can duplicate an environment in your workspace as many times as needed.

Name Use
baseUrl Environment URL
apiKey SambaSafety Credentials
basicAuthUsername SambaSafety Credentials
basicAuthPassword SambaSafety Credentials
bearerToken SambaSafety Bearer Token

Collection Variables

Name Use
groupId A group's unique identifier
personId A person's unique identifier
licenseId A license's unique identifier
activityId An activity data's unique identifier
attachmentId An attached document's unique identifier
userId A user's unique identifier
orderId A order's unique identifier
reportId A report's unique identifier

Test Scripts

This collections contains some predefined groovy scripts to collect the key id variables to update variables in this collection.

pm.test("Order Created", () => {
    pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(201);
    pm.response.to.have.header("Content-Type");
    pm.collectionVariables.set("orderId", pm.response.json().orderId);
});

request.description:
Description

This endpoint allows you login and obtain a bearer token from SambaSafety.

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

  • Authorization: Basic [encoded Client ID & Client Secret]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

  • grant_type (string, required): The type of credentials. client_credentials

  • scope (string, requied): The scope being requested. API

Response

Upon successful addition of the group, the API will respond with 200 OK containing a token.

  • token_type (string): The type of token issued.

  • expires_in (number): The time-to-live (seconds) for the token.

  • access_token (string): The token to be used for future calls.

  • scope (string): The scope granted.

item.description:
Our Authentication approach is based on an agreement with our customers that access to SambaSafety protected resources will be by way of secure server to server interactions between our customers and SambaSafety. In addition, we understand that the customer is the resource owner so no end-user authorization to SambaSafety protected resources is needed. Given these criteria, we have adopted the oAuth2 Client Credential flow.

SambaSafety APIs will not be exposed directly through a browser, tokens issued by SambaSafety will not be shared outside of a secure network and client credentials (e.g. clientId and clientSecret) will not be shared outside of a network and will be managed in secure storage. API calls are secured with transport layer encryption and client credentials are encrypted at rest using AES 256

We will return 401 Unauthorized responses to any request made from a domain that is not a SambaSafety domain when requests originate from a browser. This is enforced through CORS policies.

Any risk exposure would be the result of a customer’s security perimeter being exploited by an attacker to obtain a token or gain access to the client credentials.

Based on this more limited exposure, we have adopted a token expiration of 1 hour. In the event that there is an exploit, we also expose an API endpoint that will allow an authorized client to revoke a token.

Our API Gateway is in place to monitor and log traffic to the API.

ApiKeys

An API Gateway Key is a code used to identify and authenticate an application attempting to access the API. SambaSafety will issue you an API Gateway Key for your integration.

ClientID & ClientSecret

A set of application credentials, similar to Basic Auth: Username & Password. They are typically are generated for a API rather than an individual user.

Bearer Token

Authentication to SambaSafety's REST API is performed via HTTP Bearer Auth. Provide your API key as the Bearer token key value.

  • All API requests must be made over HTTPS.
  • Calls made over plain HTTP will fail.
  • API requests without authentication will also fail.

Warning

Your credentials carry many privileges, so be sure to keep them secure! Do not share your secret API key in publicly access.

item.name: Risk Assessment
License History Discovery

header.description: (Required) The unique identifier of the platform organization

request.description:
Description

Place an order for a license history discovery report.

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

  • productId (string, required): The state product code. "DL" is the default value.

  • subType (string, required): The state's sub type of MVR. ["3Y", "5Y", "7Y", "EM", "DB", "CR"]

  • host (string, required): The method of ordering. ["ONLINE", "OVERNIGHT"]

  • purpose (string, required): The purpose for requesting the MVR. ["EMPLOYEMENT", "INSURANCE"]

  • licenseState (string, required): The state jurisdiction issuing the document, US State Abbreviation.

  • licenseNumber (string, required): The number of the document. License Number Patterns

  • birthDate (string, date, required): The person's date of birth. "YYYY-MM-DD"

  • lastName (string(40), required): The person's family name, as indicated on the document.

  • firstName (string(40), required): The person's given name, as indicated on the document.

  • middleName (string(20), optional): The person's middle name or initial, if indicated on the document.

  • gender (string, optional): The person's gender: ["M, F, X"]

  • ssn (string, optional): The person's social security number. ["4","9"] digits without dashes.

  • billCode (string(100), optional): A customer's custom billing code.

  • billReference (string(250), optional): A customer's custom billing reference note.

  • stateAccessCode (string, optional): CA, PA, and UT require access codes.

  • reportFormats (string, options): The format of the report. Obsolete, use Accept Headers.

  • yearsRequired (string(2), required): The number of required years of confirmed driving history.

Response

Upon successful request, the API will respond with the a 201 Created containing the order ID.

  • orderId (string, uuid): The order's unique identifier.

request.description:
Description

This endpoint retrieves summary information for the corresponding order ID. The request does not include a request body.

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

  • orderId the unique identifer for the order.

Response

Upon successful request, the API will respond with details for the corresponding order. Contains the orderStatus and a links reference to the report, when completed.

Parameters:

  • orderId (string, uuid): The order's unique identifier.

  • status (string): The status of the order.

  • orderDateTime (string, datetime): The timestamp of the order.

  • orderCompletedDateTime (string, datetime): The timestamp of the order was completed.

  • mvrsOrdered (array): An object containing a Link to an MVR Report if ordered.

    • rel (string): The relationship of the link.

    • href (string): The URL of the link.

    • type (string): The HTTP Method used to access the link.

    • id (string): The unique identifier associated with the link.

  • finding (string): The findings of the request.

  • result (object): The license object containing:

    • code (string): Order result code.

    • message (string): Order result message.

  • source (string): A SambaSafety source for the order.

  • historyDate (string, date): The source date of the data.

Receive Order Completion Notification

If you have subscribed to the webhook when the order has been successfully "fulfilled", the CallbackURL will be invoked with a "POST" and a body containing a url link to the report, and the report uuid.

  • lhdorder.received

vnd.sambasafety.qorta.licensehistory.received+json

Parameters:

  • eventId (string, uuid): The callback event's unique identifier.

  • createdDateTime (string, date): The callback event's timestamp.

  • data (object): The order summary object containing:

    • orderId (string, uuid): The order's unique identifier.

    • orderDateTime (string, datetime): The timestamp of the order.

    • links (array): An array of links related to the order.

      • rel (string): The relationship of the link.

      • href (string): The URL of the link.

      • type (string): The HTTP Method used to access the link.

      • id (string): The unique identifier associated with the link.

  • eventType (string): The callback event name.

item.description:
The License History Discovery service interrogates SambaSafety’s proprietary datasets using the personal identifiers submitted to locate records that can verify license history. It fills the void where states do not provide the true license history for an individual. It can optimize workflows and speed up onboarding of drivers for companies.

How it Works

  • Authentication: Obtain a token to gain access

  • Place an Order: Place an order to get data for the person

  • Check Order Status: Check whether an order that has been placed has been fulfilled

For more information on License History Discovery visit our SambaSafety Knowledge Base

item.name: License Number Search

header.description: (Required) The unique identifier of the platform organization

request.description:
Description

Search for a drivers license number (DLN) in our database.

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

  • birthDate (string, date, required): The person's date of birth. "YYYY-MM-DD"

  • lastName (string(40), required): The person's family name, as indicated on the document.

  • firstName (string(40), required): The person's given name, as indicated on the document.

  • middleName (string(20), optional): The person's middle name or initial, if indicated on the document.

  • address (object, required): An address object containing:

    • street (string, required): The person's mailing street address.

    • city (string, required): The person's mailing municipality.

    • state (string(2), required): The person's mailing state, US State Abbreviation.

    • zipCode (string, required): The person's mailing postal code.

  • billCode (string(100), optional): A customer's custom billing code.

  • billReference (string(255), optional): A customer's custom billing reference note.

Response

Upon successful request, the API will respond with the a 201 Created containing the order ID.

  • orderId (string, uuid): The order's unique identifier.

  • licenseNumber(string): The full driver's license number.

  • licenseState (string): The license's issuing state.

  • licenseMask (string): A masked version of driver's license number.

  • status (string): A status for the result.

How to Interpret the Response

A successful response is broken down into three statuses.

  • Success containing the Full License Number and a Masked (last four digits) License Number.

  • Multiple Match if multiple potential licenses were detected for a requested driver.

  • Not Found if we can not locate a matching license in our database.

header.description: (Required) The unique identifier of the platform organization

request.description:
Description

This endpoint retrieves list of previouss orders placed for the Service. The request does not include a request body. Upon successful request, the API will respond with a list of previously placed orders, including the current order status.

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

  • page:the page of transactions to review. Default value: 1

  • size:the number of transactions to review on a page. Default value:25

  • startOrderDate: Start date when orders were created. If value is not provided, search will default to midnight (00:00:00 a.m.) of previous day.

  • endOrderDate Inclusive end date when orders were created. If value is not provided, search will default to end of day (23:59:59 p.m.).

Response

Parameters:

  • data

    • errorMessage (string): An error message attached to the order.

    • orderId (string, uuid): The license's unique identifier.

    • status (string): The enrollment type.

    • request (object): The order request object from Place an Order.

    • createdDateTime (string, datetime): The timestamp of the order.

  • meta

    • totalPages (number): The total number of pages.

    • totalRecords (number): The total number of records.

  • links

    • self (string, url): The URL to the current page.

    • first (string, url): The URL to the first page of data.

    • next (string, url): The URL to the next page of data.

    • prev (string, url): The URL to the previous page of data.

    • last (string, url): The URL to the last page of data.

Response

application/vnd.sambasafety.json;version=2.0.4

Parameters:

  • Record

    • DlRecord

      • Criteria(object): Contains parameters sent with the request.

        • OrderDate(object): Contains the date parameters of when the order was placed.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

        • OrderTime(object): Contains the time parameters of when the order was placed.

          • Hour(string): The time's hour component [0-23].

          • Minute(string): The time's minute component [0-59].

          • Second(string): The time's second component [0-59].

        • AccountID(string): The account the order was placed under.

        • UserID(string): The account user who placed the order.

        • Routing(string): An internal system routing id.

        • TrackingNumber(string): An internal system tracking number.

        • Host(string): The internal service identifier.

        • ProductID(string): The internal product code for the order.

        • State(object): The license state provided in the request.

          • Abbrev(string): The state's abbreviation.

          • Full(string): The state's full name.

        • Subtype(string): A code indicating a product subtype.

        • SubtypeFull(string): The full name for the product subtype.

        • FirstName(string): The first name provided in the request.

        • LastName(string): The last name provided in the request.

        • BirthDate(string): The birth date provided in the request.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

      • Result(object): Contains the results of the order.

        • Control(string): An internal control number for the order.

        • Valid(string): A [Y,N] indicator that the order was valid.

        • ErrorCode(string): A code for associated with an error.

        • ErrorDescription(string): A message describing the result.

        • ReturnedDate(object): Contains the date parameters of when the order was returned.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

        • ReturnTime(object): Contains the time parameters of when the order was returned.

          • Hour(string): The time's hour component [0-23].

          • Minute(string): The time's minute component [0-59].

          • Second(string): The time's second component [0-59].

        • ResultCode(string): A code for the result.

      • LicenseValidation(object): An object representing the license validation results.

        • DocumentValidationResult(string): A [PASS/FAIL] indicator on the overall document validation.

        • MatchError(string): A field name that had a match error.

        • DriverLicenseNumberMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if license numbers match.

        • BirthDateMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if birth dates match.

        • LastNameExactMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if last name exactly matches.

        • LastNameFuzzyPrimMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if last name fuzzy matches.

        • LastNameFuzzyAltMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if last name fuzzy matches.

        • FirstNameExactMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if first name exactly matches.

        • FirstNameFuzzyPrimMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if first name fuzzy matches.

        • FirstNameFuzzyAltMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if first name fuzzy matches.

        • MiddleNameExactMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if middle name exactly matches.

        • MiddleNameFuzzyPrimMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if middle name fuzzy matches.

        • MiddleNameFuzzyAltMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if middle name fuzzy matches.

        • MiddleNameInitialMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if middle initial exactly matches.

        • NameSufixMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if suffix exactly matches.

        • DocumentCategoryMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if document category matches.

        • IssueDateMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if issue date matches.

        • ExpiryDateMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if expiration date matches.

        • SexMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if gender matches.

        • HeightMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if height matches.

        • WeightMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if weight matches.

        • EyeColorMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if eye color matches.

        • Address1Match(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if address line 1 matches.

        • Address2Match(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if address line 2 matches.

        • AddressCityMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if address city matches.

        • AddressStateMatch(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if address state matches.

        • AddressZip5Match(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if address zipcode first 5 digits match.

        • AddressZip4Match(string): A [TRUE/FALSE] indicator if address zipcode last 4 digits match.

      • Driver(object): An object representing the driver.

        • FirstName(string): The first name of the driver.

        • MiddleName(string): The middle name of the driver.

        • LastName(string): The last name of the driver.

        • SuffixName(string): The suffix name of the driver.

      • CurrentLicense(object): A report object that contains a drivers active licenses.

        • Number(string): The current license number.

Description

This endpoint retrieves Activity History Report for the corresponding Report ID.

Headers

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Accept:

    • JSON: application/vnd.sambasafety.activityhistory+json;version=2.0.0

    • HTML: application/vnd.sambasafety.activityhistory+html;version=2.0.0

    • PDF: application/vnd.sambasafety.activityhistory+pdf;version=2.0.0

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

  • reportId: the unique identifier for the report.

Response

Upon successful request, the API will respond with the Activity History Report for the reportId and report version requested.

request.description:
Description

This endpoint creates a new order for a (State-Direct) Transactional MVR

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

  • productId (string, required): The state product code. "DL" is the default value.

  • subType (string, required): The state's sub type of MVR. ["3Y", "5Y", "7Y", "EM", "DB", "CR"]

  • host (string, required): The method of ordering. ["ONLINE", "OVERNIGHT"] : OVERNIGHT-HI, MO, and CA only

  • purpose (string, required): The purpose for requesting the MVR. ["EMPLOYMENT", "INSURANCE"]

  • licenseState (string(2), required, ALL CAPS): The state jurisdiction issuing the document.

  • licenseNumber (string(30), required): The number of the document. License Nmber Formats

  • birthDate (string, date, required): The person's date of birth. "YYYY-MM-DD"

  • lastName (string(40), required): The person's family name, as indicated on the document.

  • firstName (string(40), required): The person's given name, as indicated on the document.

  • middleName (string(20), optional): The person's middle name or initial, if indicated on the document.

  • gender (string, optional): The person's gender: ["M, F, X"]

  • ssn (string, optional): The person's social security number. ["4","9"] digits without dashes.

  • customfields (Array[object], optional): A customer's custom fields. Enterprise Only

    • name (string(50), optional): Value that triggers customer scoring.

    • value (string(255), optional): Value that triggers customer scoring.

  • billCode (string(100), optional): A customer's custom billing code.

  • billReference (string(250), optional): A customer's custom billing reference note.

  • stateAccessCode (string (20), optional): CA and PA require access codes. Can be sent in a request or set up on the backend.

  • originationId (string(40),optional): pass to access smart sync capability. [1-40 alphanumeric characters]

  • customerOrgId (string(20), optional): Utah only. Identifies the customer placing the order directly. Include this field when your organization is ordering an MVR for one of your own

  • subvendorOrgId (string(20), optional): Utah only. Identifies the partner organization placing an order on behalf of a customer. Include this field, along with the customer's customerOrgId, when you're a partner or reseller ordering an MVR in Utah on a customer's behalf.

Response

Upon successful request, the API will respond with the a 201 Created containing the order ID.

Parameters:

  • orderId (string, uuid): The order's unique identifier.

This endpoint retrieves summary information for the corresponding order ID. The request does not include a request body.

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Response

Upon successful request, the API will respond with details for the corresponding order. Contains the orderStatus and a links reference to the report, when completed.

Parameters:

  • mvrOrderId (string, uuid): The order's unique identifier.

  • orderStatus (string): The status of the order.

  • orderDateTime (string, datetime): The timestamp of the order.

  • license (object): The license object containing:

    • licenseState (string): The license's issuing state.

    • licenseNumber (string): The license's document number.

  • subType (string): A SambaSafety identifier for the order.

  • billCode (string): A customer's custom billing code.

  • billReference (string): A customer's custom billing reference note.

  • links (object): An array of links related to the order.

    • rel (string): The relationship of the link.

    • href (string): The URL of the link.

    • type (string): The HTTP Method used to access the link.

    • id (string): The unique identifier associated with the link.

Receive Order Completion Notification

If you have subscribed to the webhook when the order has been successfully "fulfilled", the CallbackURL will be invoked with a "POST" and a body containing a url link to the report, and the report uuid.

If an error occurs, the response will have an “error" event type, with a description of the error.

application/vnd.sambasafety.json;version=2.0.4

Parameters:

  • Record

    • DlRecord

      • Criteria(object): Contains parameters sent with the request.

        • OrderDate(object): Contains the date parameters of when the order was placed.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

        • OrderTime(object): Contains the time parameters of when the order was placed.

          • Hour(string): The time's hour component [0-23].

          • Minute(string): The time's minute component [0-59].

          • Second(string): The time's second component [0-59].

        • AccountID(string): The account the order was placed under.

        • UserID(string): The account user who placed the order.

        • Routing(string): An internal system routing id.

        • TrackingNumber(string): An internal system tracking number.

        • Host(string): The internal service identifier.

        • ProductID(string): The internal product code for the order.

        • State(object): The license state provided in the request.

          • Abbrev(string): The state's abbreviation.

          • Full(string): The state's full name.

        • Subtype(string): A code indicating a product subtype.

        • SubtypeFull(string): The full name for the product subtype.

        • FirstName(string): The first name provided in the request.

        • LastName(string): The last name provided in the request.

        • BirthDate(string): The birth date provided in the request.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

        • OrderLookBackEndDate(string): The look back date determined from the request.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

      • Result(object): Contains the results of the order.

        • Control(string): An internal control number for the order.

        • Valid(string): A [Y,N] indicator that the order was valid.

        • ErrorCode(string): A code for associated with an error.

        • ErrorDescription(string): A message describing the result.

        • ReturnedDate(object): Contains the date parameters of when the order was returned.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

        • ReturnTime(object): Contains the time parameters of when the order was returned.

          • Hour(string): The time's hour component [0-23].

          • Minute(string): The time's minute component [0-59].

          • Second(string): The time's second component [0-59].

        • ReportPeriod(string): A description of the report period.

        • CompanyClass(string): A company class code used for custom scoring.

        • CompanyScore(string): A company score assigned for custom scoring.

        • IsClear(string): A [Y, N] clear indicator.

        • IsFromArchive(string): A [Y, N] vault record indicator.

        • InvoicePath(string): The invoice path.

        • ResultCode(string): A code for the result.

      • Driver(object): An object representing the driver.

        • FirstName(string): The first name of the driver.

        • MiddleName(string): The middle name of the driver.

        • LastName(string): The last name of the driver.

        • SuffixName(string): The suffix name of the driver.

        • BirthDate(object): Contains the date parameters for the birth date of the driver.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

        • Age(string): The age of the driver.

        • EyeColor(string): The eye color of the driver.

        • HairColor(string): The hair color of the driver.

        • Weight(string): The weight of the driver.

        • Height(string): The height of the driver.

        • Gender(string): The gender of the driver.

        • Deceased(string): A [Y,N] indicator if the driver is deceased.

        • AddressList(array): An array representing addresses.

          • Street(string): The street address.

          • City(string): The city where the address is located.

          • State(string): The state where the address is located.

            • Abbrev(string): The state's abbreviation.

            • Full(string): The state's full name.

          • Zip(string): The postal code for the address.

        • ConfidenceMatch(string): The confidence score of the discovered driver.

        • LicenseNumber (string) The discovered license number.

      • LicenseHistoryList(array): A report object that contains a drivers historic licenses.

        • Type(string): Type of license, for example personal, commercial, identification.

        • ClassDescription(string): Detailed license class description type.

        • ClassCode(string): The state's license class code.

        • IssueDate(object): Contains the date parameters of when the license was issued.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

        • ExpirationDate(object): Contains the date parameters of when the license will expire.

          • Year(number): The date's year component.

          • Month(number): The date's month component.

          • Day(number): The date's day component.

          • Full(string): The date in string format.

          • Ticks(number): The date's numeric equivalent.

        • StatusList(array): A response element contains information on the status of the license.

          • Name(string): Driver's license status name.

          • Explanation(string): Additional status information from the state.

item.description:
The foreign License Discovery service allows a customer to verify if a driver has ever had a US license. The primary use case is for insurers to limit premium leakage and risk exposure by confirming if a foreign driver has ever held a US license.

CA and TX are the only states that support this product as these states see high numbers of foreign drivers that claim to not have US drivers licenses.

How it Works

  • Authentication: Obtain a token to gain access

  • Place an Order: Place an order to get data for the person

  • Check Order Status: Check whether an order that has been placed has been fulfilled

  • Get a Report: Get the data ordered

For more information on License Discovery visit our SambaSafety Knowledge Base

item.description:
The Activity Indicator service interrogates SambaSafety’s proprietary datasets using the personal identifiers submitted to locate records that can verify license activity, enabling insurance carriers to reduce data spend and improve underwriting efficiencies, and optimize workflows and speed up onboarding of drivers for companies.

  • Checks for new activity from the order date of the last MVR or vault record, up to a 3 year look back.

  • Provides “Activity” or “Clean” indicator to note if there is activity since the previous MVR order date, thus eliminating fees associated with ordering records on clean drivers.

How it Works

  • Authentication: Obtain a token to gain access

  • Place an Order: Place an order to get data for the person

  • Check Order Status: Check whether an order that has been placed has been fulfilled

  • Get a Report: Get the data ordered

For more information on Activity Indicator visit our SambaSafety Knowledge Base

item.description:
The Activity MVR service will attempt to return a historical MVR if one is available. The system will check state activity or court data for new activity.

  • If no new activity is found AND no historical MVR is available, it will return a Clean Stub.

  • If activity is found, then an MVR is ordered.

How it Works

  • Authentication: Obtain a token to gain access

  • Place an Order: Place an order to get data for the person

  • Check Order Status: Check whether an order that has been placed has been fulfilled

  • Get a Report: Get the data ordered

For more information on Activity MVR visit our SambaSafety Knowledge Base

Description

This endpoint creates a new order for an Intelligent MVR Report, for a single driver.

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

  • purpose (string, required): The purpose of the order. ["EMPLOYMENT", "INSURANCE"]

  • licenseCategory (string, required): The document's category, License Category.

  • licenseState (string, required): The state jurisdiction issuing the document, US State Abbreviation.

  • licenseNumber (string, required): The person's family name, as indicated on the document.

  • birthDate (string, date, required): The person's date of birth.

  • lastName (string, required): The person's family name, as indicated on the document.

  • firstName (string, required): The person's given name, as indicated on the document.

  • middleName (string, optional): The person's middle name or initial, if indicated on the document.

  • suffix (string, optional): The person's family suffix, Suffix.

  • address (object, optional): An address object containing:

    • street (string): The person's mailing street address.

    • city (string): The person's mailing municipality.

    • state (string): The person's mailing state, US State Abbreviation.

    • zipCode (string): The person's mailing postal code.

  • gender (string, optional): The person's gender, Gender.

  • height (number, optional): The person's height.

  • weight (number, optional): The person's weight.

  • eyeColor (string, optional): The person's eye-color, Eye-Color.

  • issueDate (string, date, optional): The document's issue date.

  • expiryDate (string, date, optional): The document's expiration date.

  • options (Array[string], optional): A list of bundled options. i.e. "LICENSE_VALIDATION"

  • customFields (Array[object], optional): A customer's custom fields.

  • billCode (string, optional): A customer's custom billing code.

  • billReference (string, optional): A customer's custom billing reference note.

  • vaultAge (number, optional): Integer value for vault age in days.
    Values accepted:

    • 0 = no vault allowed

    • 1-1095 = days

Response

Upon successful request, the API will respond with the a 201 Created containing the order ID.

Parameters:

  • orderId (string, uuid): The order's unique identifier.

item.description:
The Intelligent MVR service utilizes SambaSafety’s proprietary datasets using the personal identifiers submitted
to locate records that can verify license activity and/or violations.

  • Provides an initial Baseline MVR with first order.

  • All orders placed after the baseline MVR for the person will perform an activity check, ordering a state MVR only when new activity is present.

  • If no activity, report returned indicating driver activity check is clear.

How it Works

  • Authentication: Obtain a token to gain access

  • Place an Order: Place an order to get data for the person

  • Check Order Status: Check whether an order that has been placed has been fulfilled

  • Get a Report: Get the data ordered

For more information on Intelligent MVR visit our SambaSafety Knowledge Base

request.description:
Description

This endpoint retrieves list of previouss orders placed for the Service. The request does not include a request body. Upon successful request, the API will respond with a list of previously placed orders, including the current order status.

Headers

  • Content-Type: application/json

  • Authorization: Bearer [Token]

  • Accept: application/json

  • X-Api-Key: [ApiKey]

Request

Parameters:

Request

  • licenseCategory (string, required): The document's category, License Category.

  • licenseState (string, required): The state jurisdiction issuing the document, US State Abbreviation.

  • licenseNumber (string, required): The person's family name, as indicated on the document.

  • birthDate (string, date, required): The person's date of birth.

  • lastName (string, required): The person's family name, as indicated on the document.

  • firstName (string, required): The person's given name, as indicated on the document.

  • suffix (string, optional): The person's family suffix, Suffix.

    • city (string): The person's mailing municipality.

    • state (string): The person's mailing state, US State Abbreviation.

    • zipCode (string): The person's mailing postal code.

  • gender (string, optional): The person's gender, Gender.

  • height (number, optional): The person's height.

  • weight (number, optional): The person's weight.

  • eyeColor (string, optional): The person's eye-color, Eye-Color.

  • issueDate (string, date, optional): The document's issue date.

  • expiryDate (string, date, optional): The document's expiration date.

  • options (Array[string], optional): A list of bundled options. i.e. "LICENSE_VALIDATION"

  • customFields (Array[object], optional): A customer's custom fields.

  • billCode (string, optional): A customer's custom billing code.

  • billReference (string, optional): A customer's custom billing reference note.

  • activityDuration (number, optional): The number of months of activity.

Upon successful request, the API will respond with the a 201 Created containing the order ID.

          • Day (number) The date's day component.

        • AccountID (string) The account the order was placed under.

        • UserID (string) The account user who placed the order.

        • Routing (string) An internal system routing id.

        • TrackingNumber (string) An internal system tracking number.

        • Host (string) The internal service identifier.

        • ProductID (string) The internal product code for the order.

        • State (object) The license state provided in the request.

          • Abbrev (string) The state's abbreviation.

          • Full (string) The state's full name.

        • Subtype (string) A code indicating a product subtype.

        • SubtypeFull (string) The full name for the product subtype.

        • FirstName (string) The first name provided in the request.

        • LastName (string) The last name provided in the request.

        • BirthDate (string) The birth date provided in the request.

          • Year (number) The date's year component.

          • Month (number) The date's month component.

          • Day (number) The date's day component.

          • Full (string) The date in string format.

          • Ticks (number) The date's numeric equivalent.

        • LicenseNumber (string) The license number provided in the request.

      • Result (object) Contains the results of the order.

        • Control (string) An internal control number for the order.

        • Valid (string) A [Y,N] indicator that the order was valid.

        • ErrorDescription (string) A message describing the result.

        • ReturnedDate (object) Contains the date parameters of when the order was returned.

          • Year (number) The date's year component.

          • Month (number) The date's month component.

          • Day (number) The date's day component.

          • Full (string) The date in string format.

          • Ticks (number) The date's numeric equivalent.

        • ReturnTime (object) Contains the time parameters of when the order was returned.

          • Hour (string) The time's hour component [0-23].

          • Minute (string) The time's minute component [0-59].

          • Second (string) The time's second component [0-59].

        • IsClear (string) A [Y, N] clear indicator.

        • InvoicePath (string) The invoice path.

        • ResultCode (string) A code for the result.

      • MessageList (array) A list of messages returned as part of the report.

        • Line (string) A message line.

      • EventList (array) A list of events returned as part of the report.

        • Common (object) A set of common parameters for the event.

          • State (object) The state where the event occured.

            • Abbrev (string) The state's abbreviation.

            • Full (string) The state's full name.

          • Date (object) Contains the date parameters of when the event occured.

            • Year (number) The date's year component.

            • Month (number) The date's month component.

            • Day (number) The date's day component.

        • DescriptionList (array) of descriptions associated with the event.

          • AdjudicatedDate (object) Contains the date parameters of when the event was adjudicated in court.

            • Year (number) The date's year component.

            • Month (number) The date's month component.

            • Day (number) The date's day component.

          • Avd1 (string) A SambaSafety standardized code for the event.

          • Avd2 (string) A SambaSafety standardized code for the event.

        • Violation (object) Representing the violation.

          • ViolDisposition (string) Disposition of the violation.

          • ViolStatute (string) The state's legal statute of the violation.

          • ViolDescState (string) The state's description of the violation.

          • NewViolation (string) A [Y,N] indicator if the violation is new.

        • State (object) The state where the violation occured.

          • Abbrev (string) The state's abbreviation.

          • Full (string) The state's full name.

        • Municipality (string) The local jurisdiction where the violation occured.

        • Summons (string) The summons identification.

        • Docket (string) The docket number.

        • EventCompCode (string) A event custom scoring code.

Activity Detail is used for retrieving a historical violation detail report as an alternative to a State-Direct MVR.

How it Works

  • Authentication: Obtain a token to gain access

  • Place an Order: Place an order to get data for the person

  • Check Order Status: Check whether an order that has been placed has been fulfilled

  • Get a Report: Get the data ordered

For more information on Activity Detail visit our SambaSafety Knowledge Base

Overview

We provide a variety of Data Solutions APIs, but not all are available in every state. You can find the specific APIs available for each state in our detailed table.

Here’s a brief overview of the types of Data Solutions we offer through our REST APIs:

- License Number Search
- License Discovery
- License History Discovery
- License Verification
- Activity Detail
- Activity History
- Activity Indicator
- Activity MVR
- Intelligent MVR
- Transactional MVR

For further details, you can explore the respective links provided in our documentation.

item.description:
Groups are containers of drivers that can be organized in a hierarchical structure. Each Person (Driver/Employee) must be associated with a Group. Group configuration allows users to create groups and group hierarchies to organize their roster of people. Each time a person is added to the roster, they are added to a group. Users can also be scoped to only see specific groups and group data within their account.

Design Considerations

The groupId in the path will be used to create a Person, and as a result, the groupId must be captured and maintained by your application.

An important design decision is how Groups will be utilized, and does your database have the desired hierarchical information to share with the API.

  • Create People in a Single Group

  • Create and maintain multiple Group(s) from your application.

  • Groups are used to control User access within your application.

  • Groups allow for efficient common tasks at processed within your application.

Grouping drivers when monitoring licenses can offer several advantages:

  • Risk Management: By grouping drivers based on risk levels (e.g., high-risk, medium-risk, low-risk), companies can tailor their monitoring and intervention strategies more effectively. High-risk drivers might need more frequent checks and additional training.

  • Efficiency: Grouping drivers allows for more efficient monitoring. Instead of checking each driver individually, companies can monitor groups, making the process faster and more manageable.

  • Targeted Interventions: Different groups may require different types of interventions. For example, new drivers might need more training and mentoring, while experienced drivers might benefit from periodic refresher courses.

  • Compliance: Grouping can help ensure that all drivers meet specific regulatory requirements. For instance, commercial drivers might need different checks compared to non-commercial drivers.

  • Resource Allocation: It helps in allocating resources more effectively. Companies can focus their efforts and resources on groups that need the most attention, ensuring better overall compliance and safety.

item.description:
The License Monitoring process is not complete until the license is enrolled with the State system for monitoring.The state enrollment process occurs overnight. For daily states, enrollment responses will generally occur next day. In monthly monitoring states, the enrollment response will not occur until the monthly processing run. Monthly processing generally occurs the first week of each month. The enrollment responses are described below

Success

States do not notify of a successful enrollment, except states that provide and enrollment MVR as part of the program. Enrollment MVRs are returned the day of successful state enrollment. For all other states, if a state enrollment error is not returned, then the license has been successfully enrolled.

Errors

If there is an issue with the enrollment information (e.g. DLN, State, Birthdate, Last Name), the error information is returned by the state. Each state is different, and some states acknowledge the enrollment while others do not. Additionally, the timeline for acknowledgement varies by state, but is typically the day following the API call
for enrollment (notable exception to MI, which is every other week).

Error Handling

On enrollment, we will validate the license information meets the state requirements for format and length. If the license does not pass validation, an error and error message is returned.

Update License information to correct the license enrollment error, validate the license information and update the license information. The license information can be updated using the license PUT call and licenseId.

If enrollment errors are available within the UI and through integration calls. Users can resolve state enrollment errors within Qorta or within the system of record. Additionally, the state enrollment errors can be exposed in the system of record for user review or users and review error within Qorta. States may provide additional
information in the enrollment error message.

When to enroll drivers into monitoring?

It is recommended that people be enrolled into monitoring as soon as possible after the decision to hire or contract, in order to remove the risk of creating a monitoring period gap.

The following states have enrollment MVRs and an MVR will be provided upon enrollment.

  • Texas

  • Maryland

  • New York

  • California

There are certain states with short enrollment look back windows (typically 30 days) where immediate enrollment is needed to eliminate the risk of creating a visibility gap.

  • Arkansas

  • Maine

  • Nevada

  • Virginia

  • Louisiana

The following states have enrollment fees.

  • California

  • Texas

  • New York

  • Michigan

  • Maryland

The following states require the Driver's SSN with enrollment.

  • Arizona

  • Illinois

  • New Jersey

  • Pennsylvania

Kansas

Enrollments after the 26th will not include that month in the look back. For example, if a person is enrolled 5/25/2023 then the enrollment look back will include May. If the person is enrolled 5/26/2023, then the enrollment look-back will start with June. In the scenario of enrolling on 5/26/2023 a gap in visibility will exist between 5/26 and 5/31.

Michigan

Michigan accepts enrollments on Mondays and returns the MVR on the next Monday. So, depending on when the driver is enrolled the enrollment MVR will be returned in 7-14 days.

When to unenroll drivers from monitoring?

  • When people leave are no longer employed/contracted or have moved to a non-driving roll, they should be removed from monitoring and archived within Qorta.

  • A business rule for when a driver should be unenrolled from monitoring should be defined. There are some considerations by state that could impact when a person is removed from monitoring service.

For more information on License Monitoring Enrollment visit SambaSafety Knowledge Base:

  • US License Monitoring

item.description:
A motor vehicle record (MVR) is the documentation of a person’s driving history. The information in an MVR includes information about the driver's traffic citations, vehicular crimes, accidents, driving under the influence (DUI) convictions and the number of points on the individual’s driver’s license. Additionally, these records may contain personally identifying information (PII) such as age, date of birth, gender, eye color, hair color, weight and height.

An MVR may be used by insurance companies to determine insurance rates for drivers, with those with clean records getting lower rates. Generally, insurance companies can look back five years into an individual’s MVR. The records may also be used by employers to determine the viability of a prospective employee. These records are especially important in the case of jobs involving commercial motor vehicles (CMVs).

How it Works

  • Authentication: Obtain a token to gain access

  • Place an Order for a License: Place an order to get data for the person

  • Check Order Status: Check whether an order that has been placed has been fulfilled

  • Get a Report: Get the data ordered

For more information on Motor Vehicle Reports visit SambaSafety Knowledge Base

Overview

License monitoring, also known as MVR monitoring, is a process of regularly and automatically checking the driving records of individuals over time. This monitoring is often used by employers or organizations to keep track of the driving history of their employees or drivers who operate company-owned vehicles or drive as part of their job responsibilities.

Unlike a one-time MVR check, which is conducted during the hiring process or periodically at specific intervals, license monitoring is an ongoing process that provides real-time updates on any changes to an individual's driving record. The goal of license monitoring is to ensure that drivers maintain a safe driving history and comply with traffic laws throughout their employment or involvement with the organization.

Implementing effective license monitoring involves several key steps to ensure compliance, efficiency, and risk management.

  • Centralized License Inventory: Maintain a centralized inventory of all licenses.

    • Groups

    • People

    • Licenses

  • Enrollment in Monitoring: Use monitoring to provide real-time visibility into license status and usage.

    • Enrollments

For more information on License Monitoring visit SambaSafety Knowledge Base

item.description:
The user management page can be accessed under the “settings” icon in the customer’s account, via the Qorta application. We provide customers with large numbers of users (think 15,000 users+) to manage those users in an efficient manner.

Access Control

Access control is a security technique that regulates who or what can view or use resources in the environment. It is a fundamental concept in security that minimizes risk to your business or organization.

You are able to assign roles and groups to users, to control access.

  • Roles closely align with products you have purchased.

  • Groups are a collection of people within the organization. SambaSafety allows for group visibility to a specific User, limiting visibility to only the people and licenses with-in this groupId. This allows for another form of Access Control granularity.

Additional Restrictions - Limit Personally Identifiable Information

This restrictions removes a users ability to view certain types of personally identifiable information (PII) throughout the customer account and in any report they download from the SambaSafety platform. This information includes:

  • Date of Birth

  • Drivers License Number

  • Social Security Number

For more information on User Management visit SambaSafety Knowledge Base

item.description:
Webhooks are a powerful tool for integrations, offering several advantages:

  1. Real-time Updates: Webhooks allow applications to receive real-time data updates without needing to constantly poll an API. This is efficient and reduces unnecessary network traffic.

  2. Automation: They enable automation of workflows. For example, when a specific event occurs (like a new user registration), a webhook can trigger an action (such as sending a welcome email).

  3. Integration: Webhooks facilitate seamless integration between different services and applications. They can be used to connect various tools, making it easier to build complex systems.

  4. Scalability: By using webhooks, developers can design systems that scale more effectively. Instead of having multiple clients repeatedly request data, the server pushes updates only when necessary.

  5. Cost Efficiency: Since webhooks reduce the need for constant polling, they can help lower server and bandwidth costs.
